chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Saqr al-Sa'iq narrated that Abu Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Za'ferani quoted Abil Ahvas, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba, on the authority of Abu Qisan, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Al-A'amash, on the authority of Amr ibn Marrah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Malik al-Zubaydi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, that Abu Sufyan was riding a camel of his, Muawiyah was leading it, and Yazid was driving it, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the rider, the leader, and the driver.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبُ: The rider (one sitting on the animal)
key_terms.السَّائِقُ: The driver (one driving the animal from behind)
key_terms.القَائِدُ: The leader (one guiding the animal's head/direction)

ai.seo_question: Who did the Prophet curse regarding the camel riding arrangement of Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah, and Yazid?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights a specific incident where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cursed the rider, leader, and driver, a tradition often interpreted by Shia scholars as a prophetic foreshadowing of the roles of Abu Sufyan, Muawiyah, and Yazid during the Umayyad era. The triad of 'rider, leader, and driver' is seen not merely as a literal description of camel transport but as a symbolic archetype for authority, command, and execution, underscoring the spiritual and political dynamics of early Islamic leadership.
